transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Saturday, July 25. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. CWG: Jhandu Kumar wins India's first medal; day 2 brings mixed results in Glasgow. Jhandu Kumar opened India's medal account by winning bronze in the men's heavyweight para powerlifting event. Trump returns to White House Correspondents' dinner months after shooting forced delay. President Trump attended the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association dinner. This event followed a shooting incident outside the original venue in April. The president addressed journalists from major news organizations after months of media clashes. The dinner celebrated press freedom and raised money for journalism scholarships. Google expands in Miami after Page and Brin's $225m Florida homes; leased space quadruples. Google co-founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page have bought waterfront homes worth over $225 million in Florida. Their company, Google parent Alphabet, has also expanded its Miami office space significantly. The tech giant increased its leased office footprint more than fourfold recently. This expansion may have followed the billionaires' establishment of their new Florida residences. Setback for Trump: US appeals court refuses to revive $100,000 H-1B visa fee. A federal appeals court refused to lift a ruling blocking a $100,000 H-1B visa fee. The court left in place a decision finding the fee unlawful while the government challenges it. Democratic attorneys general argued the administration created a new tax without congressional approval. A district judge agreed, ruling the fee exceeded executive branch authority. Students' protest: Could breakthrough with Sonam Wangchuk help govt tackle crisis?. NEW DELHI: Government is keeping its fingers crossed after its successful attempt to persuade activist Sonam Wangchuk - whose wide recognition helped expand the reach of Cockroach Janta Party's protest into uncomfortable territory for BJP - to break his hunger strike. 12.5 percent to 10 percent : Why Trump admin imposed reduced tariff rate on India and what it means. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced the revised tariffs on 60 economies on Thursday, one day before the expiry of the temporary additional 10 percent duties that had been imposed on imports from all countries. Why was Tony Romo arrested? Former Cowboys star faces unexpected legal trouble in Wisconsin. Tony Romo was arrested in Milwaukee on suspicion of driving under the influence after deputies stopped his vehicle on Interstate 43. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback was booked and later released, with a court appearance set for September 21. Officials have not released toxicology results or explained why the traffic stop happened. CBS declined to comment. UK PM picks three new Indian-origin MPs from 2024 intake to join front bench. TOI correspondent from London: Three Indian-origin young Labour MPs elected at the July 2024 general election have been given front bench roles in UK PM Andy Burnham's new govt. CJP-Centre 3rd round of talks today; PM Modi, Wangchuk release late night video. NEW DELHI: The stand-off between the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the alleged NEET paper leak continued on Friday, with no breakthrough on the protesters' key demand for the resignation of union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. 4 moose released in 1904 became 200,000 and changed Newfoundland forests. A century after just four moose were released in Newfoundland to attract hunters, the introduced animals transformed the island's forests and wildlife management. Their population grew to nearly 200,000 before habitat damage triggered declines. A new management plan explains how science is now helping keep moose numbers in balance with forests, public safety and long-term ecosystem health. NY mayor hires Lina Khan who went after Amazon, Meta and Google in her days as FTC head. New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has roped in Lina Khan to lead the board of directors for the New York City Economic Development Corporation (EDC). The former chair of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) known for her aggressive antitrust lawsuits against Big Tech. According to Business Insider, Mamdani called the duo a "dream team" and framed the appointments as a strategic effort to pair urban business growth with his progressive affordability agenda. Grain, not guns: MEA rejects Russia's claim on deadly ship attack that killed 4 Indians. India's Ministry of External Affairs stated the MV Golden Leo carried grain, not weapons. This contradicts Russia's assertion regarding the ship's cargo and its attack. The vessel's tragic incident resulted in the deaths of four Indian seafarers. India reiterated its concerns to Russia's foreign minister during a recent meeting.
